The normalized inverse reweighting maps every feasible θ to a balanced λ and conversely. Positive-support independence for the columns (1,pᵢ/qᵢ) leaves pairs and noncollinear triples. In a pair, the marked vectors have equal lengths by their common pair of boundary rays; the cap fractions complement and the smaller normalized multiplier weight is at least 1/(1+b). In a triple a λᵢ above 1/2 would place pᵢ in the interior, and equality invokes the exact accepted half-weight identity, followed by the elementary reweighting estimate.

In orientation-preserving coordinates the three strict weight inequalities are the three positive successive turn determinants, and the reflected turns repeat. Direct determinant signs at the three ray-pair sums give the two-cap sectors as listed. Each complement of a θᵢ is at least 1/(1+b). Any point deleted by a cut through a nonsupporting line projects from 0 into the segment joining the two marked boundary points, because they must be the endpoints of that line section. A supporting line deletes nothing. The union of deleted sets therefore has nonnegative integral of W−1/(1+b).

The three displayed normals have the stated positive relation, with coefficients 1+a−c, a+c−1, 1+c−a, and span the plane. The three edge lines and their reflections give D=T∩(−T). The reflected barycentric inequalities are ℓᵢ≤2lᵢ; each is an actual hexagon edge, hence 0<lᵢ<1/2. Corner homotheties give tᵢ², and tᵢ+tⱼ<1 gives disjointness. Their reflected-edge sections are exactly the two marked endpoints and place the corners in singleton sectors.

The cyclic endpoints are antipodes by the barycentric identity for 0; determinant signs distinguish vᵢ from the two other vertices. The positive relation with coefficients tᵢ(1−tᵢ)/(2e) holds because the coefficient of vᵢ simplifies to lᵢ, and the one-dimensional relation space forces the original orientations to be all these choices or their simultaneous reversals. The latter would make the corner sectors two-cap sectors. Central symmetry gives the e term, and the sign inequality is affine in the corner areas after clearing its positive denominator.

The derivative in qᵢ of the corner-cost average is Aᵢ(costᵢ−average)/Q. At a minimum an unequal cost forces the appropriate endpoint; a tied multiplier can move to an endpoint leaving the average unchanged. Strict positivity of the Aᵢ forces the average between distinct extreme costs. Thus the listed patterns cover singleton, two-corner and three-corner cases, including middle ties and all equal costs.

Independently verified all five identities for 9E and also the cleared square completion and discriminant by exact integer evaluation on {0,1,2,3,4} cubed (875 equalities). All differences have degree at most four in each variable, so interpolation successively in each variable proves polynomial equality. With v≤s²/4 the singleton lower bound is nonnegative and the first pair square completion is nonnegative. The second pair has positive leading coefficient except at x=y=0 and a nonpositive discriminant; at x=0<y its bracket is 7yz². Both all-corner expansions have nonnegative coefficients.

The accepted half-weight clause therefore gives unmodified cap mean exactly 1/2, including nonsmooth edges.
